ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (Public Act 2009 No 35) as amended, and the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2020 (Public Act 2020 No 16), supplemented by the Companies (Register of Ultimate Directors and Controlling Shareholders) Amendment Regulations 2023.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the certified copy, then for Hague Apostille member destinations submit to the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) Authentication Unit for an apostille; for non-member destinations, have MFAT certify the notarized document and then apply for consular legalization at the destination country's embassy or consulate in Wellington. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain an original Certificate of Good Standing from the Companies Office; if the destination is an Apostille Convention state, attach the notarized copy to the MFAT apostille application; if the destination is not a member, follow MFAT certification followed by consular legalization by the destination country's diplomatic mission in Wellington. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the New Zealand limited company, notarized by a New Zealand notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The board resolution and power of attorney are executed before a New Zealand notary; the notarial certificate is then either apostilled by the MFAT Authentication Unit for Apostille member states or, for non-member states, certified by MFAT and subsequently consular-legalized at the destination country's embassy or consulate in New Zealand. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (stamped constitution) and the company's incorporating law firm
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: A notarized true copy of the Articles of Association is submitted to the MFAT Authentication Unit for apostille if the receiving jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention signatory; for a non-signatory state, the copy is MFAT-certified and then legalized by the receiving state's consulate in Wellington. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Qualifying New Zealand registered bank authorized under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter is issued on original bank letterhead and signed by an authorized officer; if apostille is required, the signature and authority are notarized by a New Zealand notary and then apostilled by MFAT; if the destination country is not party to the Apostille Convention, the notarized letter must be certified by MFAT and then legalized at the destination country's consulate in New Zealand. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders, authorized signatories, and any beneficial owner at or above the 25% threshold must be screened continuously against the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit watchlists, OFAC SDN list, UK HM Treasury consolidated list, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2020 sanctions list. Screening includes adverse media and negative news research. If the subject is a politically exposed person (PEP), family member, or close associate, enhanced due diligence is mandatory, requiring senior management approval, documented source of wealth and source of funds, and increased transaction monitoring. Any match to designated persons, terrorist financing, or sanctioned jurisdiction blocks the formation until cleared. Screening records must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Register - Company Name Availability Search and Name Reservation Portal (administered by the Registrar of Companies, Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory register requires the company name to be expressed in English or te reo Maori using Roman characters. Non-Roman scripts must be transliterated phonetically into Roman alphabet form. The four-tier naming model consists of: Tier 1 - the required legal suffix Limited, Ltd, LP, or equivalent; Tier 2 - a distinctive name element; Tier 3 - a descriptive element linked to the proposed business scope; and Tier 4 - any sensitive or restricted token triggering prior ministerial approval. Macrons and standard English punctuation are permitted where the registry accepts them.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 10 working days of an adverse name decision, the applicant must file a written objection with the Registrar of Companies under sections 22 and 23 of the Companies Act 1993, attaching the rejection notice, a statutory declaration, a new name search result, and evidence of the applicant's distinctive goodwill or prior registration. The Registrar must give a decision within 20 working days. If the rejection is affirmed, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand by way of originating application under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016 within 20 working days of the Registrar's final decision. Legal representation is strongly recommended for the court appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is permitted for Companies Act compliance only if it is a real physical street address in New Zealand, is not a PO Box, and includes onsite reception, mail handling, and forwarding services. For the ISIC 7490 game 3D art outsourcing industry, Inland Revenue will accept a virtual office only where the company has a genuine New Zealand business substance; it will likely reject a purely address-only arrangement. New Zealand banks and PayPal may require a physical place of business, utility bill, or lease within 12 months; a virtual office without staff, records, and meeting space will increase AML/CFT enhanced due diligence and may be rejected for account opening. Therefore, for this BPO model, a serviced office with private meeting room, staffed address, and dedicated business phone is permissible, while a bare mailbox is not recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) company nameplate affixed at the registered office; (2) staff or secretary available during declared business hours; (3) statutory records, share register, UBO register and board minutes available on demand; (4) valid lease/utility evidence; (5) bank reference file maintained. Quantified risk: low, under 5% annual probability for a standard-risk creative BPO; Inland Revenue may perform unannounced verification visits if GST or PAYE anomalies arise, and the Companies Office may require evidence of registered office consent and physical presence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), as amended; principally sections 10-22 (incorporation, name, registered office and address for service), sections 42-56 (issue and allotment of shares), sections 122-140 (board governance and directors duties), and section 151 (director residency requirement).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Business Registry Services, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application filed online through the New Zealand Companies Office register, Companies Act 1993, section 12, together with any Company Constitution and signed director consents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None: The Companies Act 1993 abolishes the concept of authorised capital and permits no-par-value shares. There is no statutory minimum paid-up capital. A company must have at least one shareholder and at least one share issued. No blocked escrow bank account or capital deposit is required before or after incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED. A meeting of the board of directors of [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the Company) was duly convened and held at [registered office address], New Zealand, on [date], at [time]. Present: [Director A], [Director B] and [Director C], constituting a quorum under clause [X] of the Company constitution. The chairperson confirmed that notice of the meeting had been validly given in accordance with section 122 of the Companies Act 1993 and the Company constitution. After open discussion, the following resolutions were unanimously passed. 1. CONSTITUTION AND REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED that the constitution filed with the New Zealand Companies Office be adopted as the Company constitution; that the registered office of the Company is at [physical street address and town], New Zealand; and that the directors are authorised to file all notices required by sections 15 to 18 of the Companies Act 1993. 2. SUBSCRIPTION AND ISSUE OF SHARE CAPITAL. RESOLVED that the initial share capital be subscribed as shown in the share register; that the board approves the issue and allotment of [number] ordinary shares to [Shareholder A], [Shareholder B], and any other subscribers, for the aggregate consideration approved by the directors; that the shares be created as no-par-value shares fully paid up and ranking equally in voting, dividend, and winding-up rights; and that the directors be authorised to complete the share register and issue share certificates. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED that [bank name] be appointed as the Company principal banker; that the board approves opening operating, US dollar, and settlement accounts; and that the bank mandate authorises [Director A] and [Director B] to sign jointly for all transactions. FURTHER RESOLVED that no account transaction above NZD 10,000 be initiated without a prior board authorisation recorded in the minutes. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED that [Director A] be appointed Managing Director, [Director B] be appointed Finance Director, and [name] be appointed Company Secretary; and that each such officer has authority to execute contracts, instruct external lawyers and accountants, engage banking representatives, and file records with the Companies Office and Inland Revenue Department. 5. OVERALL RATIFICATION. RESOLVED that all steps taken to incorporate the Company, including the reservation of name, preparation of the constitution, payment of the incorporation fee, and any incidental obligations, are ratified and approved as if undertaken pursuant to this resolution. This resolution takes effect immediately and remains in force until revoked by a later board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and File Incorporation Application with the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online register (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz), operated by the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a search on the New Zealand Companies Office register to confirm the proposed name is available; prepare the Company constitution and consent forms. Log into the Companies Office online portal; select incorporation; enter the company name, physical address, director and shareholder details, and confirm compliance with section 12 of the Companies Act 1993. The application must name at least one director who satisfies the section 151 residency requirement and is not disqualified. Submit the online application using the government login and authorise payment of the incorporation fee. Where a director resides outside New Zealand, attach a notarised passport copy and a completed director consent; the application is an electronic legal declaration, so certify that every detail is true and correct.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in priority order
Signed consent to act as director for each director
Statement of registered office physical address
Statement of address for service, if different
Verified identity documents for overseas directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office stops or queries the application, resubmit within 10 working days; correct any defect identified in the notice. If the chosen name is unavailable, file an amended application with the next available name. Contact the MBIE business registry helpline or use the online enquiry system to resolve the suspension before expiry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Registered Office, Address for Service and Post-Incorporation Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online update service and board of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, use the Companies Office online update service to enter or confirm the physical registered office and address for service. The registered office must be a physical location in New Zealand at which documents can be served and that is open to the public on working days; a postal box alone is not sufficient. File any changes to director or shareholder details, and adopt the statutory registers in the company minute book. Convene and record the first board meeting, adopt the pro-forma first board resolution, and lodge any director consent not already filed. The secretary should issue share certificates and make the necessary entries in the share register, director register, and shareholder register before initiating bank account opening.
required_dossiers: Shareholder information and ultimate beneficial ownership declarations
Board meeting minutes and statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office or director notices are queried, update the online register within 5 working days. If the physical office fails inspection or cannot be used for service, appoint a registered agent or certified address provider and file the new address immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain New Zealand Business Number and Complete Inland Revenue Department Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) Registry and Inland Revenue Department (IRD) myIR business registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation the company automatically receives a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) from the Companies Office. The board must then complete business registration with the Inland Revenue Department for income tax; register for goods and services tax (GST) if annual taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 or if voluntary registration is preferred; and register as an employer for PAYE if staff are engaged. The application is made through the Inland Revenue myIR portal using the NZBN and company details. Provide the IRD number of each director and the company postal address; state the standard balance date of 31 March unless another balance date is approved. Non-resident ownership is permitted, and no license is required for the export of digital creative services.
required_dossiers: Company extract from the Companies Office
Estimated annual turnover for GST registration
PAYE employer registration details, if hiring
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD tax registration is deferred or queried, call the Inland Revenue corporate tax contact and provide the outstanding director IRD numbers or entity details. If the GST threshold is understated, request voluntary GST registration after assessing the projected turnover; request a formal notice of assessment and correct the return via myIR.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Accounts and Execute the Banking Authorization Mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed bank under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, subject to the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: At the board level, provide the incorporating bank with the NZBN company extract, certificate of incorporation, and fully executed first board resolution concerning banking authorization. Each authorised signatory must complete standard customer due diligence under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, supplying certified copies of a passport, proof of residential address, and, for non-resident directors, notarised documents. The board should also give a brief but detailed business scope describing AAA game asset 3D sculpting and character rigging outsourcing, expected monthly transaction volume, annual turnover, and the intended use of Wire Transfer and PayPal payment rails. Instruct the bank to open operating, foreign currency, and settlement accounts. After bank acceptance, deposit any initial paid-up capital if applicable and record the transfer in the company books.
required_dossiers: Certified passports and proof of address for authorised signatories
Business plan and fee schedule describing 3D art outsourcing
Bank account application and mandate forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines or delays the account, request the bank written reasons and supplement the filing with additional evidence of legitimate business purpose, client contracts, or source of funds. If still unresolved, apply to another New Zealand licensed bank; after exhausting the bank internal complaint process, escalate to the Banking Ombudsman Scheme in New Zealand.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 7490 is a professional, scientific and technical services classification; the registered activity is a digital creative 3D art outsourcing studio, not a physical manufacturing plant, chemical works, assembly facility, or warehouse.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - New Zealand does not require an industrial operating permit for digital 3D art outsourcing, character rigging, or creative game asset production. No factory or warehouse operating license is required; general duties apply under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - reference only: Environmental Protection Authority New Zealand and the territorial authority under the Resource Management Act 1991; no EIA approval is required for this service business.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - digital services generate no discharge to air, land or water; no resource consent or environmental impact assessment is triggered under Schedule 4 of the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater, VOC, particulate, or hazardous waste streams are generated by the core business. If office computer hardware is decommissioned, dispose through a Ministry for the Environment certified e-waste recycler under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defence fire permit under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017 is required because the studio does not store chemicals or operate heavy industry. Any leased office must hold a current building warrant of fitness under the Building Act 2004, and the employer must comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including first aid, workstation ergonomics, and general workplace safety obligations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand (Inland Revenue / IRD). Online portal: myIR Secure Online Services – https://www.ird.govt.nz. Administered under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A New Zealand incorporated limited company is issued an IRD number (TIN) automatically upon incorporation through the Companies Register. For foreign non-resident entities needing a statutory New Zealand TIN or GST/VAT-type registration number, the SOP is: 1) access myIR at ird.govt.nz or use the IRD prescribed non-resident application channel; 2) submit the company foreign certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, director and ultimate beneficial owner identification, registered office address, and the country-of-residence tax reference number; 3) state the intended New Zealand tax or GST activity, including expected turnover from New Zealand supplies; 4) await IRD validation, typically 5–10 working days, after which the IRD number is issued; 5) if GST registration is required, elect the myIR service ‘Register for GST’ using that TIN; 6) for non-resident suppliers of remote services to New Zealand consumers, mandatory GST registration is required once NZD 60,000 of New Zealand consumer supplies is exceeded in a 12-month period.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. New Zealand does not provide an elective check-the-box or look-through election for ordinary limited companies; the entity is taxed at corporate level. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 are mandatory and create no entity-reclassification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST – Goods and Services Tax under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: New Zealand Dollar (NZD) 60,000 of taxable supplies in any rolling 12-month period; mandatory registration once the threshold is exceeded, voluntary registration is available below it. Non-resident suppliers of remote services and low-value goods to New Zealand consumers are subject to the same NZD 60,000 threshold for their New Zealand consumer supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No statutory real-time fiscal clearance, no continuous transaction control API, and no anti-fraud digital stamping regime are currently imposed in New Zealand. E-invoicing is voluntary and aligned to the PEPPOL interoperability framework. Tax invoices must satisfy section 24 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 and may be issued and stored electronically under the Electronic Transactions Act 2002.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 provides the statutory zero-rating tests. Goods are zero-rated when they are exported from New Zealand and evidence of physical export is retained. Services are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, provided the service is not directly connected with New Zealand land or goods situated in New Zealand, and is not supplied to a person physically present in New Zealand under certain visa or residence circumstances. For this 3D game art outsourcing scope, the supply of digital artwork, 3D sculpting, rigging and any related intellectual property to a non-resident game studio is a zero-rated exported service if the customer’s business establishment and end-use are offshore and the digital deliverables are transferred electronically outside New Zealand. Substantiation must include non-resident status evidence and delivery or end-use records. There is no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline under the GST Act; adopting a 180-day remittance benchmark is recommended to demonstrate commercial substance.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Signed master services agreement or purchase order identifying the offshore game studio and the 3D art, sculpting and rigging deliverables
GST zero-rated tax invoice issued to the non-resident customer containing the supplier’s New Zealand GST registration number
Electronic delivery receipt or signed acceptance certificate for the exported digital files (e.g., ZIP, FBX, OBJ, rig assets)
Bank SWIFT MT103 or equivalent foreign-currency remittance receipt showing receipt of payment from the offshore customer
Certified evidence of the customer’s non-resident status (foreign certificate of incorporation, overseas tax identification number, or statutory declaration)
If applicable, an IP assignment or licence agreement evidencing transfer of rights for use exclusively outside New Zealand
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may reassess a zero-rated export supply as taxable at 15% GST where the section 11 conditions are not met or the substantiation bundle is deficient. The resulting shortfall accrues use-of-money interest under the Tax Administration Act 1994. Shortfall penalties under section 141 Tax Administration Act 1994 apply at 20% where the taxpayer fails to take reasonable care, 40% for a substantially below correct tax position, 100% for an abusive tax position and 150% for evasion or similar. Knowingly providing false export zero-rating documentation can trigger criminal prosecution, significant fines and imprisonment. Retrospective reassessments may be made within seven years for non-fraudulent understatements and without a time limit in cases of fraud or evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand - Te Pūtea Matua
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand has a liberalised, freely convertible currency regime under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021, with no exchange controls, no surrender requirements, and no mandatory conversion ratios. The New Zealand dollar floats freely, and both current account and capital account transactions may be settled without central bank approval. Dividend and profit remittances are subject only to standard corporate tax documentation and banking KYC checks, not to exchange control permission. Inward investment screening under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 is limited to sensitive land and significant business assets, and does not apply to ordinary operating capital for an outsourced game art studio. Foreign currency accounts can be held freely, and payment clearing can occur in NZD or major currencies such as USD, EUR, and AUD. The absence of exchange controls does not eliminate AML/CFT obligations; banks still require robust source-of-funds evidence, beneficial ownership disclosure, and transaction purpose verification. The practical consequence is that treasury structuring is driven by counterparty risk, settlement efficiency, and hedging needs rather than by state-imposed convertibility constraints.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion rules apply in New Zealand. Exporters and service providers may retain foreign currency receipts in offshore or onshore foreign currency accounts without any forced conversion timeline or ratio. Settlement occurs at freely agreed market exchange rates through authorised banking channels.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Business Account with Foreign Currency Settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs without a New Zealand financial service provider licence and AML/CFT registration are not viable for corporate treasury purposes, as they would not hold a registered banking relationship under New Zealand law. NZ-licensed non-bank payment providers and digital banks are feasible for small-value receivables such as PayPal settlements, but they are not substitutes for Tier-1 commercial bank clearing rails for large inbound capital or trade disbursements. The recommended approach is to use local Tier-1 banks as principal clearing counterparties and keep EMIs restricted to low-limit ancillary payment collection.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand does not impose a statutory requirement for directors to appear physically in-branch for company account opening. In practice, most major banks permit remote onboarding using digital identity verification, provided the entity is registered on the New Zealand Companies Register and all beneficial owners provide certified identification documents. A remote or consular-assisted verification may be accepted at the bank's discretion, but the bank retains the right to require an in-person interview for ultimate beneficial owners or for transactions above internal risk thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity involving nominee shareholders or discretionary trusts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified companies register extract, complete shareholding ledger, trust deed with settled schedules, written beneficial ownership declaration from every natural person owning 20% or more, and passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for inbound capital injection from foreign gaming or publishing counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements, bank statements for the past 12 months, signed master services agreements, purchase orders from game publishers, revenue invoices with settlement proof, and tax reconciliation showing no unexplained cash movements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP screening, or adverse media hits on third-party contractors or client counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed counterparty KYC files, sanctions screening reports at the time of onboarding, negative press search results, risk-rating memos, PEP declaration forms, and a written explanation of the commercial relationship and payment purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual payment routing where client funds originate from high-risk jurisdictions before reaching New Zealand
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full payment chain provenance, invoices tied to completed 3D art deliverables, intellectual property assignment agreements, sub-contracting evidence, payroll records, and a transactional narrative demonstrating that final beneficiaries are legitimate service providers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections should be settled by SWIFT wire transfers from the shareholder's or parent entity's bank to the New Zealand entity's Tier-1 bank account, using clear cross-border payment instructions and the correct beneficiary legal name. New Zealand has no exchange control approval requirement, but banks require the remitter to state the purpose of the payment and the recipient to provide supporting board resolutions, share allotment records, or shareholder loan agreements. If the injection is paid-up share capital, the amount is evidenced by the Companies Office share issue return and a bank confirmation letter. No statutory capital verification is required because New Zealand has no minimum paid-in capital for a limited liability company.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements, SWIFT MT103 wire transfers are the preferred clearing rail for recurring service fees, royalties, and contractor payments. Commercial letters of credit may be used for high-value imported hardware or software infrastructure purchases where supplier trust is moderate. Documentary collections are acceptable for smaller transactions with known counterparties where the cost of letter-of-credit issuance exceeds the risk. All outbound payments are cleared through the correspondent banking network in USD, EUR, or NZD, and must be protected by internal KYC checks on overseas payees and the underlying commercial contract.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla NZD/USD deliverable forward contracts with maturities up to 12 months
AUD/NZD cross-currency swaps for natural revenue-cost matching
FX options purchased from Tier-1 bank trading desks to cap adverse conversion rates

No non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible on the NZD itself because a fully deliverable onshore forward market exists; NDFs are only considered for exotic non-convertible currencies in isolated third-party settlement scenarios

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually on or before the company's registered Annual Return Date (the anniversary of the date of registration as set by the Registrar on the Companies Register); a company in default is placed under a final notice requiring filing within 20 working days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled annual returns trigger the Registrar's notice-to-remedy; if the return remains unfiled after the notice period, the Registrar may strike the company off the Companies Register, and the company and its directors face maximum fines of NZD 10,000, with continuing daily penalties of up to NZD 50 per day for non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Income Tax Return (IR4) under the Income Tax Act 2007 and Tax Administration Act 1994
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the standard 1 April to 31 March income year, the return is due by 7 July following the balance date; a registered tax agent may obtain an extension to the following 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs an initial NZD 250 late-filing penalty and NZD 50 per further month (capped at NZD 500); unpaid tax attracts an initial late-payment penalty of 5%, plus Use of Money interest and monthly incremental penalties of 1% until paid

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Goods and Services Tax Return (GST101) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Mandatory registration when taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period or start when exceeding threshold; if registered, the standard quarterly return and payment are due by the 28th day of the month after the end of the taxable period (January-March due 28 April, etc.)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register or file exposes the company to unexpected GST liability, an initial 5% late-payment penalty, further 1% monthly late-payment penalties, Use of Money interest, and late-return penalties of NZD 250 for each unfiled return

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Fringe Benefit Tax Return (IR405) under the Income Tax Act 2007
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If fringe benefits are provided to employees, the quarterly return is due by the 28th day of the month after the quarter end; an annual return for the 1 April-31 March year is due by 7 July for taxpayers that file annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and late payment attract the same IRD penalty regime as income tax: NZD 250 initial late-filing penalty, NZD 50 per month to NZD 500, plus initial 5% late-payment penalty, monthly 1% penalty interest, and Use of Money interest

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Financial Statements and Annual Report prepared under Companies Act 1993 ss 199-201 and Financial Reporting Act 2013
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; filed with the Registrar of Companies only if the company is a large company or an FMC reporting entity (otherwise maintained at the registered office and available to shareholders)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The board must provide the audited or verified financial statements and any annual report to shareholders within five months after the balance date; if the company is required to file financial statements with the Companies Office, they are due within five working days after they are provided to shareholders (or such shorter deadline prescribed)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare or provide financial statements and audit report within the five-month period is an offence; directors may be fined up to NZD 50,000 and the Registrar may order compliance; persistent default can lead to the company being struck off and disqualification of directors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Notice of Change of Registered Office, Directors, Director Details, Constitution, or Ultimate Holding Company (Companies Act 1993 ss 23, 213, 216)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each event is reported within 20 working days after the change; share transfers are recorded in the company's own share register promptly and are formally confirmed through the next annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-notification within 20 working days is a continuing default leading to registration default notices, fines of up to NZD 10,000 for the company and NZD 50,000 for officers, and eventual strike-off if the register records ongoing default

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Companies Act 1993, an independent certified auditor must be appointed when: (a) the company is an FMC reporting entity (public issuer, bank, insurer, licensed supervisor); (b) the company is a large company (any two of: total assets exceeding NZD 60 million, total revenue exceeding NZD 30 million, and 100 or more full-time equivalent employees); (c) shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares validly require an audit; (d) the constitution or another Act requires an audit; or (e) the company is a subsidiary of an existing large reporting group that needs statutory consolidated audited accounts. A small or medium company that does not meet these criteria is exempt from a mandatory statutory audit unless a shareholder requirement or a contractual lender submits a valid audit request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared in accordance with New Zealand GAAP as issued by the External Reporting Board: Tier 1 full NZ IFRS (mandatory for FMC reporting entities and large for-profit entities), Tier 2 NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime, Tier 3/4 simple-format/simplified accounting standards for eligible small/medium for-profit entities. The audit itself must follow International Standards on Auditing (New Zealand) issued by the New Zealand Auditing and Assurance Standards Board.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not have a stand-alone UBO filing register. The annual return to the Companies Office includes the current shareholding record and ultimate holding company details, serving as the principal annual confirmation of legal ownership. Share transfers must be recorded in the company's share register without delay; no 30-day Companies Office filing is required for a pure share transfer, but if the transfer affects ultimate holding company details, the change must be filed within 20 working days. AML/CFT reporting entities (not this standard low-risk services company, absent financial-service activity) must maintain beneficial-owner identity and verification information on a current basis and refresh it when facts change or at review intervals; no separate annual UBO confirmation is submitted to the Registrar.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (share register) containing the names, addresses, and allotted shares of every shareholder
Minute Book recording board resolutions, shareholder resolutions, and meeting minutes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - USD 1,500 per annum (New Zealand registered office and resident agent / compliance agent market range)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 25,000 per audit engagement for a small-to-mid-size New Zealand company

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% corporate income tax rate under Income Tax Act 2007, subpart MB, charged on the worldwide income of a New Zealand resident limited company.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand offers a 15% R&D Tax Incentive credit for eligible research and development expenditure. There is no general free-zone tax holiday and no patent box; tax losses are in principle carried forward indefinitely subject to shareholder continuity rules, but this compliance pipeline applies a conservative 5-year carryforward cap for the 3D art outsourcing business model.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return filed through the Inland Revenue myIR electronic portal, with provisional tax paid via IR219 instalments and related schedules filed under the company's IRD number.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 return must be filed no later than 7 July immediately following the balance date for electronic filers, with provisional tax instalments generally due on 28 August, 15 January and 7 May; paper filers face earlier statutory due dates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover derived from AAA game 3D sculpting, character rigging, art outsourcing and related creative BPO services supplied to overseas clients.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned New Zealand Ltd, declare gross worldwide income before expenses; convert foreign-currency invoicing to NZD using Inland Revenue approved exchange rates; exclude amounts on account of GST if the company is GST-registered; ensure income is not misclassified as foreign-sourced merely because clients are offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross interest received from bank deposits, intercompany loans, debentures and other interest-bearing instruments held by the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide interest income of the New Zealand resident company; amounts paid by the NZ entity to foreign related lenders may attract NRWT at 15% or 2% Approved Issuer Levy on interest; do not net off foreign tax before declaring the gross amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends received from New Zealand-resident companies and any foreign portfolio or controlled-company dividends, including imputation credit information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent should not expect to use imputation credits; dividends paid by this NZ Ltd to non-resident shareholders are subject to non-resident withholding tax on distribution; for inbound dividends, report the cash amount with any foreign tax credits claimed separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Royalties from licensing game assets, 3D models, animation rigs, software/IP, commissions, foreign exchange gains and any miscellaneous income not included in Box 1.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply New Zealand source rules under sections YD 4 and YD 5 of the Income Tax Act 2007; cross-border royalties paid to the NZ company for intellectual property developed in New Zealand are generally taxable in New Zealand; disclose any foreign withholding tax suffered to claim foreign tax credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Arithmetical sum of Box 1 through Box 4, being total assessable income before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should note that undistributed Box 5 income remains subject to New Zealand company tax; a later dividend distribution will generate NRWT, and no deduction is allowed for notional dividends accumulated offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses including artist salaries, software subscriptions, cloud rendering costs, subcontractor fees, rent, legal fees, marketing and other business costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only deductions satisfying the general permission in section DA 1 and the general limitations in DA 2; related-party outsourcing fees to non-resident 3D artists or group entities must be benchmarked at arm's length; non-arms'-length payments will be adjusted and penalties may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 5 minus Box 6, representing the net assessable income of the company before loss offsets and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The NZ Ltd must file a New Zealand return as a tax resident even if all ultimately profitable activity is controlled by non-resident shareholders; any attempt to shift taxable profit to an overseas shell through inflated deductions will trigger GAAR and transfer pricing adjustments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final company tax at 28% after applying available imputation credits, R&D tax incentive credits, foreign tax credits and any tax losses carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any residual tax must be paid by the terminal tax date; dividends paid to non-residents later will generate NRWT, and treaty relief cannot be claimed by the NZ company in its own return for the benefit of non-resident shareholders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a Failure to File penalty under section 139AB of the Tax Administration Act 1994 of NZD 250 per month per return (NZD 500 for large taxpayers), capped at NZD 2,500; late payment penalties under section 139A apply at 1% on day one, 2% on day eight and 1% monthly thereafter; deliberate evasion or fraudulent misstatement attracts a 100% tax shortfall penalty under sections 141 and 143A, plus criminal liability on conviction of a fine up to NZD 50,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% NZ NRWT on fully imputed dividends paid to non-residents and 30% NRWT on non-fully imputed dividends, unless a lower Double Tax Agreement rate applies; the NZ payer must withhold and account to Inland Revenue on the actual distribution, not merely on accumulated profits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident recipient must satisfy Inland Revenue that it is the beneficial owner of the payment, obtain a current Tax Residency Certificate from its home jurisdiction tax authority, complete Inland Revenue residence certification and NRWT rate application documentation (including form IR290 where applicable), submit the documents to the NZ payer before the dividend/interest/royalty payment, and ensure no treaty-shopping arrangement exists; the NZ company is required to withhold at the domestic rate until Inland Revenue confirms the reduced treaty rate, with refunds processed through the non-resident taxpayer's IRD account.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on cross-border royalty payments is 15%; under applicable DTA the royalty rate is typically reduced to 5% or 10% depending on the jurisdiction and IP type. Statutory NRWT on cross-border interest is 15%; the rate may be reduced to between 0% and 10% under a DTA, or replaced by the 2% Approved Issuer Levy if the NZ borrower is an approved issuer and the interest is on approved debentures, which converts the burden from NRWT to AIL and eliminates NRWT on that interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10 million aggregate cross-border related-party transactions requires the NZ Ltd to prepare contemporaneous Master File and Local File documentation; multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue equal to or exceeding NZD 1 billion are subject to mandatory Country-by-Country reporting in New Zealand.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand is not an Economic Substance Regulations jurisdiction in the Gulf-style sense, but the OECD substance doctrine, the New Zealand general anti-avoidance rule under section BG 1, and the Multilateral Instrument principal purpose test require the company to perform its core income-generating activities in New Zealand: actual 3D modelling, sculpting, rigging, art direction, contract negotiation and risk management must all be supported by local staff, premises, board decisions and accounting substance; a bare invoice conduit with foreign decision-makers will be treated as a sham or artificial arrangement for tax purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directors knowingly understate 3D art outsourcing revenue, fabricate overseas subcontractor invoices, inflate payroll expense, or route profits to a related entity in a zero-tax jurisdiction without economic substance or arm's-length pricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act 2007 section BG 1 and Tax Administration Act 1994 sections 141, 143A and 143B impose a tax shortfall penalty of 100% of the evaded tax, daily penal interest, and criminal prosecution with a fine up to NZD 50,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years per offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced under Companies Act 1993 section 300 for reckless trading; directors are personally liable for civil restitution of the tax shortfall and assets withheld, may be prohibited from leaving New Zealand under a travel prohibition order under section 157H of the Tax Administration Act 1994, and face criminal imprisonment up to 5 years for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a letterbox New Zealand company with no physical office, zero local employees, no actual 3D art production or rigging activities, and all strategic decisions made abroad, while claiming New Zealand treaty benefits and transferring income offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act 2007 sections BG 1 and GB 1 permit Inland Revenue to disregard the structure, reallocate profits, deny treaty benefits under the MLI principal purpose test, impose shortfall penalties up to 100%, and reassess the company and its shareholders on a reconstruction basis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors bear personal civil liability for knowingly allowing the company to trade with no legitimate business substance; courts may pierce the veil and treat the NZ Ltd as an agent or sham, directors may be disqualified from managing companies under Companies Act 1993 section 383, listed on Inland Revenue's blacklisting/non-compliance register, subjected to asset restraint and travel bans, and prosecuted criminally for fraudulent trading.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The company accepts Wire Transfer and PayPal proceeds without conducting customer due diligence or beneficial ownership verification, fails to file an AML/CFT risk assessment or compliance programme, or knowingly processes digital art licensing payments derived from ransomware, fraud, or organised crime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 imposes civil and criminal penalties on body corporates of up to NZD 2 million per contravention; individuals and directors face fines up to NZD 300,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years, and the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009 permits forfeiture of assets traceable to criminal proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal money-laundering charges under Crimes Act 1961 section 243, which carries imprisonment up to 7 years, together with civil asset recovery, travel restrictions and border alerts, disqualification from company management, and blacklisting by financial institutions which serves as a de facto travel and banking ban.
